Bulgaria votes in presidential runoff after tight first round

The vote comes against the backdrop of a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast in the past month.

A woman votes at a polling station during the second round of the presidential election, in Sofia on Nov 1, 2026. REUTERS/Spasiyana Sergieva

FAST

SOFIA: Bulgarians went to the polls on Sunday (Nov 1) to elect a president after a tight race between the two leading candidates failed to produce an outright winner in last weekend's first round vote for the largely ceremonial role. Incumbent president, Iliana Iotova, 61, led over ex-caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, but fell short of the 50 per cent threshold in the first round race of 27 candidates that saw a record-low turnout. Exit polls will be published after voting ends at 8 pm (1800 GMT), with a result likely on Monday as the ballot papers are counted. The presidential vote comes against the backdrop of a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast in the past month, which have sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of the war in Ukraine.

About two dozen seafarers are feared dead and the strikes have prompted the government to seek allied assistance to bolster maritime security. On Wednesday a Greek container ship sank after being hit by sea drones. Both leading presidential candidates have condemned the attacks. Prime Minister Rumen Radev, who backs Iotova, said the strikes' outcome "benefits the Russian Federation". They have both called for a diplomatic end to the war. A victory for Iotova would make her Bulgaria's first elected female president. She became acting president in January after Radev resigned to enter and win a parliamentary race on what many political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket. Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is supported by pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine. He signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his time as premier. A host of right-leaning political figures, among them ex-premier Boiko Borisov, have expressed support for Gyurov.

Source: Reuters/ht

FAST

SEPANG, Malaysia, Nov 1 : Reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez won the Malaysian Grand Prix on Sunday for the first time since 2018 to take a 44-point lead over absent title rival Jorge Martin in the championship. Marquez shot out of the blocks and beat his brother Alex, the pole-sitter, into the opening turn. Alex Marquez was able to quickly regain the lead but ran wide a turn later to hand it back, and his brother made no mistakes from that point on to claim the chequered flag. Victory moved seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez up to 399 points in the championship standings, 44 ahead of Martin, who did not compete after suffering a wrist fracture. If Marquez is able to extend his lead to 74 points at next week's Qatar Grand Prix, he can seal an eighth championship title with two rounds remaining in the season.

"We did a perfect race, so I'm super, super happy," said Marquez, who won the race by a commanding margin of over four seconds. "But my mentality still cannot change. I have to keep focus, keep pushing. There are not many races to go, but there are many moments left. So, we must be super confident." Saturday's sprint winner Pedro Acosta of KTM finished second, while Gresini's Alex was third. After losing the lead to his brother, Alex Marquez was drawn into a duel with Acosta, who stuck to the wheel of the Gresini rider for several laps before expertly overtaking him at the midway point of the race. By then, however, the distance to the leader had already grown too large to overcome. Aprilia rider Marco Bezzecchi, an outside contender for the title, finished in sixth place after being overtaken late by both Trackhouse rider Ai Ogura and Tech3's Enea Bastianini. MARTIN ABSENT Marquez's main title rival Martin had initially looked set to return in Malaysia and briefly attempted to compete in Saturday morning's practice session. However, the Aprilia rider was visibly struggling and eventually did not take part in qualifying, ending his weekend to continue his recovery from the fracture he sustained in the crash at Phillip Island last week. The Spaniard, who won the title in 2024, conceded that his MotoGP title challenge was effectively over after his withdrawal. The MotoGP season next moves to the Lusail International Circuit for the Qatar Grand Prix, which is set to go ahead next week despite pushback from riders concerned about going there during the war against Iran.

Source: Reuters

BEIJING, Nov 1 : Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi said on Sunday it delivered more than 50,000 electric vehicles in October, the highest monthly total this year, as it ramps up production to meet its 2026 target. Deliveries reached about 336,000 vehicles for the first 10 months after topping 30,000 units in August and 40,000 in September. The company aims to deliver 550,000 vehicles in 2026. Its January-October deliveries represent about 61 per cent of that goal.

FAST

DHAKA: Bangladesh announced a six-member wage board on Sunday (Nov 1) to review garment workers' pay and urged employees to return to work, but protests demanding higher wages continued across major industrial areas, disrupting transport and factory operations. Workers in the South Asian nation are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka (U$245), more than double the current 12,500 taka, saying rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare have sharply eroded their purchasing power. The dispute has raised concerns about disruption to an industry that employs about 4 million workers, generates more than 80 per cent of Bangladesh's export earnings and supplies clothing to many leading Western brands. Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said the wage board was formed after discussions with workers' representatives and industry leaders and urged workers to resume work.

Despite the announcement, thousands of garment workers staged fresh demonstrations on Sunday. Police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse workers who had blocked a busy intersection in Dhaka, police said. Some protesters hurled bricks at officers during the clashes. Hundreds of workers also blocked a major highway in Gazipur, on the outskirts of the capital, disrupting transport in one of the country's key industrial belts. The demonstrations forced owners to shut 25 to 30 factories, while authorities deployed Border Guard Bangladesh personnel to maintain order, Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Amjad Hossain said. The latest unrest follows demonstrations in Ashulia, a major garment manufacturing hub on the outskirts of Dhaka, where dozens of factories suspended operations on Saturday after workers staged protests demanding higher pay. Chowdhury warned that prolonged disruptions could delay export shipments and payments from international buyers, creating further difficulties for manufacturers and workers alike. Bangladesh's ready-made garment industry, the world's largest after China, contributes about 10 per cent of gross domestic product and is the backbone of the economy. Manufacturers, however, said the sector is facing mounting challenges, including rising production costs, periodic gas and electricity shortages, and uncertainty in energy markets linked to tensions in the Middle East.

Source: Reuters/ht

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines said on Sunday (Nov 1) that some customer information may have been affected by a cybersecurity incident involving Amadeus, its reservation-technology provider. The airline joins Cathay Pacific Airways, Japan Airlines, South Korea’s Asiana Airlines and others in recent days that have reported customer data was compromised in the Amadeus breach. Malaysia’s flag carrier said in a statement that the incident may have affected information processed between August 2023 and September 2026. The airline said it is working with Amadeus and relevant parties to investigate the incident and assess its impact.

FAST

NEW DELHI: Indian security personnel carrying batons and shields and accompanied by riot control vehicles surrounded the site of a planned opposition protest in Delhi on Sunday (Nov 1) that is set to demand the resignation of the country's election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.  Authorities warned of traffic diversions ahead of the protest march and rally that will be led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi.  The opposition says it expects hundreds of thousands of people to participate in what it says will be a major challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).  Opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have held near-daily demonstrations since last month demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar step down over the voter list revision that critics say favour the BJP.

The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.  Analysts say the youth protests, and growing support for the opposition, form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014. But his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029. The opposition parties have announced they will hold a nearly 1.5 km march on Sunday from Central Delhi to the Ramlila Maidan, a ground that is the designated site for their protest rally. Visuals from news agency ANI showed riot control vehicles and dozens of security personnel armed with batons and shields outside the rally venue, where announcements were being made urging people to ensure smooth traffic movement and cooperate with police officials.  Delhi Traffic Police said "a large gathering" was expected at the venue, and traffic regulations and diversions would be implemented "as required".  "People have started coming to participate in this rally...we have ensured proper arrangements at the venue, and arrangements are also planned on the route of the march that will happen in a few hours from now," senior police officer Rohit Rajbir told ANI.  The protests demanding Kumar's resignation erupted after The Indian Express newspaper reported in September that his two deputies had raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures, and digital systems.  The change, which began last year, removed over 130 million names - more than the population of Japan- from voter lists, including 28 million who died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced. Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party - allegations the poll panel and BJP reject.

Source: Reuters/ht

FAST

Nov 1 : MotoGP officials told teams on Sunday they had received no information warranting a change to the Qatar Grand Prix, which is to go ahead next week despite pushback from riders concerned about going there during the war against Iran. The race at the Lusail International Circuit, originally scheduled for April, was postponed to November 6 to 8 due to the conflict, which has spread through much of the region, beyond the initial US-Israeli attacks on Iran. A group of riders had sought more assurances over travel to the Gulf region, such as details on evacuation plans and indemnity insurance. "This morning MotoGP management met with the teams to review the latest information and assurances provided by the State of Qatar, Lusail International Circuit, relevant embassies and independent experts," a MotoGP spokesperson told Reuters.

"These internal and external assessments continue to inform our ongoing risk review and decision-making process. "Following a review of the latest information, official assurances from the State of Qatar and independent assessments available to us at this moment, we have received no information that would warrant a change to the current plans for the event." MotoGP added the safety and well-being of everyone in the paddock "remains our highest priority" ahead of the season's final race in Asia before the series returns to Europe for the last two rounds in Portugal and Valencia. "We will continue to monitor developments closely and remain in regular contact with all relevant authorities and stakeholders," the spokesperson said. "Decisions of this nature must be based on the most current facts, advice from official sources and informed assessment available at the time they are made. Should that assessment change, we will act accordingly." The International Road Racing Teams Association, which represents all MotoGP teams and helps in coordinating paddock logistics, also attended the meeting. Qatar has guaranteed that teams would not be stranded in case of any escalation in the conflict. Aprilia and Ducati, the two leading constructors in the championship this season, have confirmed they would travel to Qatar. Ducati's championship leader Marc Marquez and Aprilia's Jorge Martin are the leading contenders for the title, with the two Spaniards separated by 19 points ahead of Sunday's race in Malaysia. A person with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters that all teams except Yamaha have committed to travelling to Qatar, with the Japanese outfit awaiting instructions following a Japanese government advisory that urged citizens to refrain from non-essential travel to the Gulf nation. Teams are responsible for ensuring their riders attend the Qatar Grand Prix. However, it is the governing body of motorcycle racing, FIM, that will decide whether to punish riders who do not show up.

Source: Reuters

FAST

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Lewis Hamilton recalled Ferrari's glory years with Michael Schumacher as one seven-time Formula One world champion harked back to another on Saturday with his first pole position for the Italian team. The achievement at Mexico City's Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez was the Briton's first pole since July 2023 and first, apart from in two sprint races, since his arrival at Maranello from Mercedes. It was also a record-extending career 105th and made him, at 41, the oldest pole-sitter since Mario Andretti, then 42, at Monza in 1982. Germany's Schumacher, who retired at Mercedes in 2012 and won five titles with Ferrari from 2000 to 2004, had his first pole for Ferrari at the 1996 San Marino Grand Prix.

"It feels great to be able to reward them with a pole. And to have your first Ferrari pole, I mean, it just takes me back to watching Michael get all those pole positions when he was at Ferrari and all those wins. So, it's very, very special," said Hamilton. The Briton, who won in Spain this year to become Formula One's oldest winner since Australian Jack Brabham in 1970, suggested age was all in the mind. "I ice bath a lot. I do all those different things that you can do to try and keep yourself young and fit. Yeah, but I love what I do, and that love has not gone," he said. "I wake up every day thinking about it. I dream about it. And I've got this amazing support around the world. These guys keep me going, and so I hope they're happy with that today, and I hope that I can deliver for them tomorrow." Sunday looks set to crown Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli as the youngest ever champion, at 20 years old.  Antonelli starts fourth and needs only finish in the top nine to take the title, and not even that if Hamilton or Mercedes' George Russell fails to win. Hamilton is 124 points behind with a maximum 100 to win after Mexico, and Russell is 123 off the lead.   The Italian replaced Hamilton at Mercedes, and the Briton spoke warmly of his admiration for what the "little kid" he recalled standing at the back of the garage had achieved. "I think it's really, really great to see. And also, records are there to be broken, you know," said Hamilton. "He's just got such a bright future ahead of him. So, I'm grateful that I can be racing in the time to see it, to witness it. I do hope in the future we get to have some actual battles because we didn't get to have any battles this year."

Source: Reuters
